# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code and Codex when a beads workspace is resolved

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```



## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: stealth mode (no git ops)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

commands.name: wb:create_design
commands.description: (Workbench) Write docs/plans/<project>/design.md: WHAT to build and WHY — decisions, rationale, scope, success criteria, risks — from validated research. Use when research.md is complete and the user asks to design, decide the approach, or write the design doc, or to formalize a decision explore_design recorded. Does not plan implementation steps. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: wb:create_handoff
commands.description: (Workbench) Write a handoff document that carries this session's working context — decisions, discoveries, deviations from plan, beads state, next steps — into a new session, model, or agent. Use when ending or pausing a session, switching models or machines, when asked to hand off, checkpoint, or save context, or before compaction on long-running work. Takes the project directory under docs/plans/ and an optional reason.

commands.name: wb:create_mockup
commands.description: (Workbench) Research existing UI patterns and produce an initial mockup for a feature, with clarifying questions for the user. Use when the user asks for a mockup, wireframe, or UI draft for a planned feature; iterate afterwards with mockup-iteration. Takes the project directory and a feature description.

commands.name: wb:create_product_research
commands.description: (Workbench) Research a codebase from the product perspective — features, user flows, user-visible behaviors — into research.md written in product language. Use when the research question is about what the software does for users rather than how the code works, or when a PM-facing write-up is requested. Takes the project directory and the question.

commands.name: wb:create_project
commands.description: (Workbench) Start a new wb project: create docs/plans/<date>-<name>/ with README, research.md, design.md, and tasks.md skeletons and record git metadata. Use when the user wants to plan, scope, or kick off a feature, refactor, or investigation as a tracked project, or asks to set up plan docs. First stage of the workflow; research follows. Takes a project name and optional base directory and ticket.

commands.name: wb:create_research
commands.description: (Workbench) Research how something currently works in this codebase and write docs/plans/<project>/research.md: facts only, file:line references, no recommendations. Spawns parallel locator, analyzer, and pattern-finder agents. Use when a project directory exists and the user asks to research, investigate, document, or understand current behavior, or before design when research.md is missing or stale. Takes the project directory and the research question.

commands.name: wb:create_tasks
commands.description: (Workbench) Turn an approved design.md into docs/plans/<project>/tasks.md: phased, executable tasks with file:line targets and verification, plus the beads epic, milestones, task issues, and dependencies. Use when design is approved and the user asks to plan the implementation, break the work down, create tasks, or set up beads for a project. Recommended on Fable. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: wb:explore_design
commands.description: (Workbench) Facilitated architecture discussion between research and design: explores directions as possibilities, converges only on explicit user approval, and records the decision durably (thoughts/ doc plus a closed Decide: issue). Use when a design has open trade-offs or competing directions, or the user wants to think through options before committing; skip when the decision is already made. Recommended on Fable. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: wb:help
commands.description: (Workbench) Reference for the wb workflow and, in a repository with an active plan, where you are and what's next: which documents exist and their status, epic and milestone state, open Q: and Decide: issues, what the next stage needs from you, and what the previous stage left undone. Use when the user asks where they are, what's next, what a stage needs, or how wb works. Takes an optional topic.

commands.name: wb:implement
commands.description: (Workbench) Implement a project's tasks.md by coordinating fresh-context worker agents (one per task, model chosen per task), verifying each with a task-verifier, and escalating verified failures. The default execution path: use when the user asks to implement, build, or execute a planned phase, asks for workers or coordination, or wants the main context kept clean. Takes the project directory and a phase number or continue.

commands.name: wb:implement_inline
commands.description: (Workbench) Implement a project's tasks.md in this session with TDD (red, green, refactor), beads claim and close per task, and a human checkpoint at each phase boundary. Use only when the user asks for the work done inline, in this session, or on the session model rather than by workers (for example a full-Fable run). Takes the project directory and a phase number or continue.

commands.name: wb:mockup-iteration
commands.description: (Workbench) Iterate on UI mockups, capturing keeps/removes/changes with full fidelity. Versions each iteration and maintains decision log.

commands.name: wb:research-validation
commands.description: (Workbench) Validate a research document (research.md or product-research.md) against the current codebase: file paths exist, code snippets match, behavioral claims hold. Use when the user asks to validate, verify, or fact-check research, or asks whether research is still accurate after the code changed. Takes an optional project directory.

commands.name: wb:resume_handoff
commands.description: (Workbench) Resume work from a handoff document written by create_handoff: reload the context, decisions, discoveries, and next steps, then continue from the ready work in beads. Use at the start of a session when the user points at a handoff file or asks to pick up, resume, or continue prior work. Takes the handoff file path.

commands.name: wb:review-prep
commands.description: (Workbench) Interactive pair-programming walkthrough of a diff using tmux and nvim: opens each changed file in an nvim pane and takes questions as you go. Use when the user wants to be walked through what changed, to understand a diff by reading it together, or to prep a PR that way; not for an automated review that reports bugs or security findings.

commands.name: wb:update_status
commands.description: (Workbench) Reconcile a wb plan's documentation status from beads — the sole writer of tasks.md frontmatter progress fields (status, current_phase, completed_tasks) and the status lines in research.md and design.md. Use when a phase or task set completes, when asked to update, sync, or reconcile plan status or progress, before a handoff, or when a plan's frontmatter looks stale against bd state. Takes the project directory under docs/plans/.

commands.name: wb:validate_execution
commands.description: (Workbench) Validate that an implemented plan matches design.md and tasks.md: run the automated checks, compare the implementation to the requirements, and produce a pass/fail report with gaps. Use after a phase or project is implemented when the user asks to validate, verify, or review whether the plan was done correctly. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: wb:validate_project
commands.description: (Workbench) Check that a docs/plans/<project>/ directory follows the wb workflow: required files, frontmatter, status transitions, beads tracking, and stage ordering. Use when plan documents look inconsistent, when asked to validate or audit a project's docs, or before resuming an old project. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: beads:beads
commands.description: (beads) Dolt-powered issue tracker for multi-session work with dependencies and persistent memory across conversation compaction. Use when work spans sessions, has blockers, or needs context recovery after compaction. Trigger with "create task", "what's ready", "track this work", "resume after compaction". Make sure to use this skill whenever managing multi-session work, tracking dependencies, or recovering context.

commands.name: typesafe:typesafe-ai
commands.description: (typesafe) Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits. Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.

commands.name: cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer
commands.description: (cowork-plugin-management) Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration.

commands.name: cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin
commands.description: (cowork-plugin-management) Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. Use when users want to create a plugin, build a plugin, make a new plugin, develop a plugin, scaffold a plugin, start a plugin from scratch, or design a plugin. This skill requires Cowork mode with access to the outputs directory for delivering the final .plugin file.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. commands.name: wb:implement_inline
commands.description: (Workbench) Implement a project's tasks.md in this session with TDD (red, green, refactor), beads claim and close per task, and a human checkpoint at each phase boundary. Use only when the user asks for the work done inline, in this session, or on the session model rather than by workers (for example a full-Fable run). Takes the project directory and a phase number or continue.

commands.name: wb:mockup-iteration
commands.description: (Workbench) Iterate on UI mockups, capturing keeps/removes/changes with full fidelity. Versions each iteration and maintains decision log.

commands.name: wb:research-validation
commands.description: (Workbench) Validate a research document (research.md or product-research.md) against the current codebase: file paths exist, code snippets match, behavioral claims hold. Use when the user asks to validate, verify, or fact-check research, or asks whether research is still accurate after the code changed. Takes an optional project directory.

commands.name: wb:resume_handoff
commands.description: (Workbench) Resume work from a handoff document written by create_handoff: reload the context, decisions, discoveries, and next steps, then continue from the ready work in beads. Use at the start of a session when the user points at a handoff file or asks to pick up, resume, or continue prior work. Takes the handoff file path.

commands.name: wb:review-prep
commands.description: (Workbench) Interactive pair-programming walkthrough of a diff using tmux and nvim: opens each changed file in an nvim pane and takes questions as you go. Use when the user wants to be walked through what changed, to understand a diff by reading it together, or to prep a PR that way; not for an automated review that reports bugs or security findings.

commands.name: wb:update_status
commands.description: (Workbench) Reconcile a wb plan's documentation status from beads — the sole writer of tasks.md frontmatter progress fields (status, current_phase, completed_tasks) and the status lines in research.md and design.md. Use when a phase or task set completes, when asked to update, sync, or reconcile plan status or progress, before a handoff, or when a plan's frontmatter looks stale against bd state. Takes the project directory under docs/plans/.

commands.name: wb:validate_execution
commands.description: (Workbench) Validate that an implemented plan matches design.md and tasks.md: run the automated checks, compare the implementation to the requirements, and produce a pass/fail report with gaps. Use after a phase or project is implemented when the user asks to validate, verify, or review whether the plan was done correctly. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: wb:validate_project
commands.description: (Workbench) Check that a docs/plans/<project>/ directory follows the wb workflow: required files, frontmatter, status transitions, beads tracking, and stage ordering. Use when plan documents look inconsistent, when asked to validate or audit a project's docs, or before resuming an old project. Takes the project directory.

commands.name: beads:beads
commands.description: (beads) Dolt-powered issue tracker for multi-session work with dependencies and persistent memory across conversation compaction. Use when work spans sessions, has blockers, or needs context recovery after compaction. Trigger with "create task", "what's ready", "track this work", "resume after compaction". Make sure to use this skill whenever managing multi-session work, tracking dependencies, or recovering context.

commands.name: typesafe:typesafe-ai
commands.description: (typesafe) Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits. Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.

commands.name: cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer
commands.description: (cowork-plugin-management) Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration.

commands.name: cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin
commands.description: (cowork-plugin-management) Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. Use when users want to create a plugin, build a plugin, make a new plugin, develop a plugin, scaffold a plugin, start a plugin from scratch, or design a plugin. This skill requires Cowork mode with access to the outputs directory for delivering the final .plugin file.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

# Research: Rides Window and Check-in Focus

**Created**: 2026-10-20
**Last Updated**: 2026-10-20
**Ticket**: N/A

## Research Question

How does the rides page choose which rides to show, and how does the check-in wizard advance between questions?

## Summary

The rides page is built as an HTML string in `rides/views.py`. It lists rides through `list_rides` in `rides/store.py`, which keeps rides inside a window set by the constant `WINDOW_DAYS = 27`. The window start is computed as today minus `WINDOW_DAYS - 1` days, so the oldest listed ride is 26 days before today.

Distances are shown through `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py`, which rounds to one decimal with Python's built-in `round`. The check-in wizard is static HTML plus a script: a click on an answer hides the current question and unhides the next one, and no code sets focus.

Tests run with pytest only. There is no browser test harness, no Playwright or Selenium configuration, and no test of the wizard.

## Intent Coverage

Against the README Intent's "Success looks like" statements:

- **Statements the findings bear on**: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed" — the window constant and cutoff in `rides/store.py:4-9`; "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — the click handler in `wizard/wizard.js:6-16`
- **Statements the findings do not touch**: none

## Detailed Findings

### Rides window

**Location**: `rides/store.py`

**What exists**:

- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` ([`rides/store.py:4`](rides/store.py))
- `list_rides(rides, today)` computes `cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` and keeps rides with `cutoff <= date <= today`, newest first ([`rides/store.py:7-11`](rides/store.py))
- `load_series(rides, today)` counts rides per week for four weeks ([`rides/store.py:14-21`](rides/store.py))

**How it works**:

1. `render_rides_page` in `rides/views.py:6-11` calls `list_rides` and renders one `<li class="ride">` per ride.
2. With `today` = Oct 28, the cutoff is Oct 2, so a ride on Oct 1 is not listed.

### Distance display

**Location**: `rides/view_model.py`

**What exists**:

- `format_distance(km)` returns `f"{round(km, 1)} km"` ([`rides/view_model.py:4-6`](rides/view_model.py))
- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` both call it ([`rides/views.py:8`](rides/views.py), [`rides/views.py:16`](rides/views.py))

### Check-in wizard

**Location**: `wizard/`

**What exists**:

- Three `fieldset.question` elements; the second and third start `hidden` ([`wizard/wizard.html:5-19`](wizard/wizard.html))
- A click handler per answer button stores the value, hides the current question, and unhides the next ([`wizard/wizard.js:6-16`](wizard/wizard.js))
- No call to `focus()` and no `tabindex` handling anywhere in `wizard/`

## Architecture Documentation

**Current patterns found**:

- Pages are plain string builders: `rides/views.py:6-17`
- Display formatting lives in `rides/view_model.py`, separate from the views

**Component connections**:

- `rides/views.py` → `rides/store.py`: listing (`rides/views.py:9`)
- `rides/views.py` → `rides/view_model.py`: distance text (`rides/views.py:8`)

**Conventions observed**:

- A ride is a dict with `date` and `km` keys.

## Open Questions

- None.

18	2. **Ties round to even.** `format_distance` uses built-in `round` (`rides/view_model.py:6`), so 12.25 km shows as 12.2 km where riders expect 12.3 km.
19	3. **No day total.** The today page lists each ride's distance and nothing else (`rides/views.py:14-17`).

24	- **M2**: A distance exactly halfway between two tenths displays rounded up. (refines: amendment "distances round half up (12.25 km shows 12.3 km)")

27

29	
30	- **Window**: change `WINDOW_DAYS` from 27 to 28 and keep the inclusive cutoff formula.

64	- The day total on the today page

# Design: Rides Window, Distance Rounding, and Today's Total

## Problem Statement

README Goal (with the 2026-10-20 amendment): the rides page shows the last 28 days of rides inclusive, distances round half up, and the today page shows the day's total distance.

1. **Rides window is one day short.** `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` and the cutoff `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` list today plus 26 prior days (`rides/store.py:4-10`). On Oct 28 a ride on Oct 1 is missing.
2. **Ties round to even.** `format_distance` uses built-in `round` (`rides/view_model.py:6`), so 12.25 km shows as 12.2 km where riders expect 12.3 km.
3. **No day total.** The today page lists each ride's distance and nothing else (`rides/views.py:14-17`).

### Success Metrics

- **M1**: On Oct 28 the rides page lists Oct 1 through Oct 28 inclusive. (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not (on Oct 28, a ride on Oct 1 is listed and one on Sep 30 is not)")
- **M2**: A distance exactly halfway between two tenths displays rounded up. (refines: amendment "distances round half up (12.25 km shows 12.3 km)")
- **M3**: The today page shows the sum of today's distances. (refines: amendment "the today page shows the day's total distance")
- Deferred: "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" (amendment: wizard work moves to a later project)

## Design Approach

- **Window**: change `WINDOW_DAYS` from 27 to 28 and keep the inclusive cutoff formula.
- **Rounding**: `format_distance` rounds through `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, converting the float with `str(km)` first. An `int` stays whole (`5` shows `5 km`) and a float keeps its one decimal (`10.0` shows `10.0 km`).
- **Day total**: `render_today_page` adds a `Total: <distance>` line after the list, formatted with `format_distance`.

### Why This Approach

- Each change is local to one function (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`; `rides/views.py:14-17`)
- Display formatting already lives in `rides/view_model.py`, so the total reuses it (research: Patterns)
- `Decimal(str(km))` rounds the decimal the rider entered. `Decimal(km)` would round the binary float, and a float such as 1.15 is stored just below 1.15

## Technical Decisions

### Architecture

- Keep the string-built pages
  - Rationale: no page structure change beyond one line on the today page
  - Trade-off: none
  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`

### Data Model

- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`

### Integration Points

- `render_rides_page` picks up both the window and the rounding through its existing calls
- `render_today_page` gains the total line

## Scope Definition

### In Scope

- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`
- The day total on the today page

### Out of Scope

- The check-in wizard
- `load_series`
- Any new page

## Success Criteria

### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1 A ride 27 days before today is listed on the rides page and one 28 days before is not**
  - Given today is 2026-10-28
  - When the rides page is rendered with rides on 2026-10-01 and 2026-09-30
  - Then the page lists the 2026-10-01 ride and not the 2026-09-30 ride
  - Example: rides on 2026-10-01 (10.0 km) and 2026-09-30 (8.0 km), today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `2026-10-01` and does not contain `2026-09-30`
  - Example (edge): a ride dated today, 2026-10-28, is listed
  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
  - Refines: M1

- **AC-2 A distance halfway between two tenths rounds up on the rides page**
  - Given a ride today of 12.25 km
  - When the rides page is rendered
  - Then the ride shows as 12.3 km
  - Example: a ride on 2026-10-28 of 12.25 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `12.3 km`
  - Example (edge): a ride of 1.15 km shows as `1.2 km`
  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
  - Refines: M2

- **AC-3 The today page shows the day's total distance**
  - Given rides today and on other days
  - When the today page is rendered
  - Then it shows the sum of today's distances only
  - Example: rides on 2026-10-28 of 10.0 km and 2.5 km and one on 2026-10-27 of 7.0 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `Total: 12.5 km`
  - Observed at: `render_today_page` HTML
  - Refines: M3

### Harness Decisions

| Boundary | Harness present? | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rides page HTML (`render_rides_page`) | pytest (`pyproject.toml:10-12`, `tests/`) | Use as is |
| Today page HTML (`render_today_page`) | pytest (`tests/test_today_page.py`) | Use as is |

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Performance: no change
- [ ] Reliability: existing tests pass, except expectations this design changes
- [ ] Security: not applicable

## Risk Analysis

### Technical Risks

| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Float values round unexpectedly | Low | Med | Convert with `Decimal(str(km))`; a test pins 1.15 → 1.2 km |
| A trailing `.0` is lost | Low | Low | Do not `normalize()` the Decimal; a test pins 10.0 → 10.0 km |

### Assumptions

- Distances are positive numbers.

## Open Questions

- None.

## References

- Research: [research.md](research.md)
- Intent: [README.md](README.md)

"""In-memory ride listing. A ride is a dict with a `date` (datetime.date) and `km` (float)."""
from datetime import timedelta

WINDOW_DAYS = 28


def list_rides(rides, today):
    """Return rides from the recent window, newest first."""
    cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)
    recent = [r for r in rides if cutoff <= r["date"] <= today]
    return sorted(recent, key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)


def load_series(rides, today):
    """Count rides per week, most recent week first, for the last four weeks."""
    counts = []
    for week in range(4):
        end = today - timedelta(days=7 * week)
        start = end - timedelta(days=6)
        counts.append(len([r for r in rides if start <= r["date"] <= end]))
    return counts

```python
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def format_distance(km):
    """Distance as a display string, rounded half up to one decimal, e.g. 12.3 km."""
    if isinstance(km, int):
        return f"{km} km"
    value = Decimal(str(km)).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return f"{value} km"
```

content.content:
The rides page lists 28 days inclusive (AC-1), ties round up (AC-2), and the today page shows the day's total (AC-3).

### Prerequisites

- [ ] Research validated
- [ ] Design approved
- [ ] Development environment ready: a Python 3.10 or later with pytest

### Changes Required

#### 1. Rides window

**File**: `rides/store.py`

**Current State** (from research.md):

- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` at line 4; `list_rides` computes the cutoff at line 9

**Target State** (design.md M1):

- Today plus the 27 prior days

**Implementation**:

```python
# At line 4, replace:
WINDOW_DAYS = 27

# With:
WINDOW_DAYS = 28
```

**Rationale**: the cutoff is `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)`, so 28 gives 28 days inclusive.
**Pattern Reference**: `rides/store.py:18-19` (the same `N - 1` closed-range idiom)

#### 2. Distance rounding

**File**: `rides/view_model.py`

**Current State** (from research.md):

- `format_distance` uses built-in `round` at line 6

**Target State** (design.md M2):

- 12.25 displays as `12.3 km` and 1.15 as `1.2 km`
- A whole-number (int) input stays whole (`5` shows `5 km`), and a float keeps its one decimal (`10.0` shows `10.0 km`)

**Implementation**:

```python
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def format_distance(km):
    """Distance as a display string, rounded half up to one decimal, e.g. 12.3 km."""
    if isinstance(km, int):
        return f"{km} km"
    value = Decimal(str(km)).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return f"{value} km"
```

  - Example (edge): a ride of 1.15 km shows as `1.2 km`
  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
  - Refines: M2

- **AC-3 The today page shows the day's total distance**
  - Given rides today and on other days
  - When the today page is rendered
  - Then it shows the sum of today's distances only
  - Example: rides on 2026-10-28 of 10.0 km and 2.5 km and one on 2026-10-27 of 7.0 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `Total: 12.5 km`
  - Observed at: `render_today_page` HTML
  - Refines: M3

| --- | --- | --- |

content.content:
1	# Test Quality Reference
2	
3	Supporting material for the [test-quality](SKILL.md) rubric: a detector method with worked examples, heuristics for what no linter detects, and the shape of a review finding.
4	
5	## Detector selections
6	
7	This section gives a method that works in any ecosystem, then worked examples of the method for a few stacks. The examples are not a supported list: a stack that is absent from the table (Mocha, node:test, or any other) gets the same method, and skipping the detector step silently because the stack is unlisted hides defects the rubric exists to catch.
8	
9	### Method
10	
11	1. Find the project's own tools. Read the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) for the linters, test runner, and mutation or coverage tools already in use. Run only what is installed in the project and never install anything, because a tool the team has not adopted produces findings the team cannot act on.
12	2. Select rules by category, using explicit selections rather than the project's configured rule set, because many of the highest-signal rules are off by default and a configured lint run misses them. The core categories the examples cover include: assertion-free tests, always-true or no-op assertions, skipped or focused tests, duplicate tests or titles, stubs of the subject, mocking beyond the subject (any-instance stubs, message chains, stubbed mocks), test-data and setup cost (factory cascades, unneeded persistence), sleeps and wall-clock waits, over-broad exception assertions, and conditional logic in tests. Other rule families a stack's linter offers (for example leaked state, async misuse, oversized snapshots) are selected the same way. Report rules that are available but not enabled separately from violations. Read the lint configuration only for thresholds, and run size rules (such as `RSpec/MultipleExpectations` and `RSpec/ExampleLength`) at the project's thresholds or exclude them, because their defaults conflict with common team guidance.
13	3. Add the runtime checks the stack offers when the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) gives a runnable command for them: seeded random order, repeat runs on suspect tests only, a slow-test report, a factory or setup-cost profile, and per-test coverage. Run a mutation tool only when that source declares its command. Report any check not run, with the reason.
14	4. Where a category has no detector in the stack, report "no detector for <category> in this stack" and fall back to the rubric and the custom heuristics below, labelled judgment-only. Do not omit the category and do not guess at rule names.
15	5. Include what was found (tools, selections, rules available but not enabled, categories with no detector) in your report, so the testing profile or Testing Conventions can be updated from it and the next run starts from it.
16	
17	### Worked examples
18	
19	These rows show the method applied to six stacks; they are examples, not the only supported stacks. No source publishes false-positive rates for any of these rules; the noise notes are inferences.
20	
21	| Stack | Static selection (default status) | Runtime and suite checks | Known noise |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| RSpec | rubocop-rspec `RSpec/SubjectStub`, `AnyInstance`, `MessageChain`, `StubbedMock`, `NoExpectationExample`, `VoidExpect`, `IdenticalEqualityAssertion`, `UnspecifiedException`, `Be`, `RepeatedExample`, `RepeatedExampleGroupBody`, `LetSetup`, `Focus`, `LeakyConstantDeclaration` (all enabled by default); rubocop-factory_bot `FactoryBot/ExcessiveCreateList`, `FactoryAssociationWithStrategy` (pending) | TestProf `FPROF=1` (total vs top-level factory counts expose cascades), `FDOC=1` (unnecessary persistence), `RD_PROF=1`; `--seed` plus `rspec --bisect`; `mutant --since <ref>` if configured | `MultipleExpectations`, `ExampleLength`, `MultipleMemoizedHelpers`, `NestedGroups` are noisy; `VerifiedDoubles` medium. `FDOC` reports "potential" offenders |
24	| Minitest | rubocop-minitest `Minitest/UselessAssertion`, `AssertWithExpectedArgument`, `UnreachableAssertion`, `TestMethodName`, `DuplicateTestRun` (pending), `NoAssertions` (disabled) | `FPROF` and `FDOC` also work under Minitest | No equivalent of `SubjectStub`; mocking needs the heuristics below |
25	| pytest | `ruff check --select PT,B011,B017 --output-format json`, excluding style-only `PT006`, `PT007`, `PT001`, `PT023` and `S101`. Only `PT010`, `PT014`, `PT020`, `PT025`, `PT026`, `PT031` are enabled by default | `--durations`; pytest-randomly seeded order; pytest-repeat or flakefinder on suspects only; coverage contexts for overlap; mutmut if configured | No assertion-free-test rule and no static sleep rule; the heuristics below fill in |
26	| Jest / Vitest | Recommended: `expect-expect`, `no-conditional-expect`, `no-standalone-expect`, `valid-expect`, `no-identical-title`, `no-disabled-tests`, `no-focused-tests`. Opt-in: `no-conditional-in-test`, `no-large-snapshots`, `require-to-throw-message`, `max-expects` | `--randomize --seed`; Stryker `--incremental` | `expect-expect` misfires on custom assertion helpers until `assertFunctionNames` is set |
27	| Playwright / Testing Library | Playwright recommended covers `no-wait-for-timeout`, `no-force-option`, `no-networkidle`, `prefer-web-first-assertions`; `expect-expect` and `no-unnecessary-assertions` are opt-in. Testing Library `await-async-*`; `prefer-explicit-assert` is opt-in | none listed | Bare `getBy*` asserts implicitly, which confuses `expect-expect` |
28	| Go | testifylint `useless-assert`, `expected-actual`, `require-error` (on by default) | gremlins on small modules | gremlins is still 0.x |
29	
30	The selections come from the rubocop-rspec, rubocop-factory_bot, rubocop-minitest, Ruff, eslint-plugin-jest, @vitest/eslint-plugin, eslint-plugin-playwright, eslint-plugin-testing-library, and testifylint documentation.
31	
32	## Custom heuristics
33	
34	No linter in any ecosystem detects mocking volume or a mirrored oracle. Check these with grep or an AST helper, and present each hit as "review these" with line evidence, because each needs judgment to confirm and has no validated threshold:
35	
36	- stubs of the subject, or of ActiveRecord, outside RSpec;
37	- interaction-only assertions (only `have_received` or `toHaveBeenCalled`-style assertions in a test);
38	- assertions on source text or CSS class strings;
39	- `sleep` or wall-clock bounds;
40	- expected values that call production helpers;
41	- assertion-free tests in Python.
42	
43	## Review finding
44	
45	Each finding from a reviewer or auditor has these fields:
46	
47	- **Verdict**: Remove, Rewrite, Consolidate, or Keep (rubric Part 3).
48	- **Rubric item**: the Part 1 item, or the Part 2 property and item.
49	- **Location**: file:line and a quoted excerpt.
50	- **Evidence type**: deterministic (the named detector, planted defect, or diff) or judgment-only.
51	- **Majority**: for a judgment-only Remove or Rewrite, the majority result (for example 3 of 3).
52	- **Objective evidence**: for Remove or Consolidate, the evidence (no unique killed mutants, or no unique coverage, plus a passing run with the test removed in a disposable worktree), or "judgment-only, not actionable".
53	- **Criterion**: the criterion id, when the review runs inside a plan.

1	---
2	project: rides

8	
9	# Research: Rides Window and Check-in Focus
10	
11	**Created**: 2026-10-20
12	**Last Updated**: 2026-10-20
13	**Ticket**: N/A
14	
15	## Research Question
16	
17	How does the rides page choose which rides to show, and how does the check-in wizard advance between questions?
18	
19	## Summary
20	
21	The rides page is built as an HTML string in `rides/views.py`. It lists rides through `list_rides` in `rides/store.py`, which keeps rides inside a window set by the constant `WINDOW_DAYS = 27`. The window start is computed as today minus `WINDOW_DAYS - 1` days, so the oldest listed ride is 26 days before today.
22	
23	Distances are shown through `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py`, which rounds to one decimal with Python's built-in `round`. The check-in wizard is static HTML plus a script: a click on an answer hides the current question and unhides the next one, and no code sets focus.
24	
25	Tests run with pytest only. There is no browser test harness, no Playwright or Selenium configuration, and no test of the wizard.
26	
27	## Intent Coverage
28	
29	Against the README Intent's "Success looks like" statements:
30	
31	- **Statements the findings bear on**: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed" — the window constant and cutoff in `rides/store.py:4-9`; "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — the click handler in `wizard/wizard.js:6-16`
32	- **Statements the findings do not touch**: none
33	
34	## Detailed Findings
35	
36	### Rides window
37	
38	**Location**: `rides/store.py`
39	
40	**What exists**:
41	
42	- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` ([`rides/store.py:4`](rides/store.py))
43	- `list_rides(rides, today)` computes `cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` and keeps rides with `cutoff <= date <= today`, newest first ([`rides/store.py:7-11`](rides/store.py))
44	- `load_series(rides, today)` counts rides per week for four weeks ([`rides/store.py:14-21`](rides/store.py))
45	
46	**How it works**:
47	
48	1. `render_rides_page` in `rides/views.py:6-11` calls `list_rides` and renders one `<li class="ride">` per ride.
49	2. With `today` = Oct 28, the cutoff is Oct 2, so a ride on Oct 1 is not listed.
50	
51	### Distance display
52	
53	**Location**: `rides/view_model.py`
54	
55	**What exists**:
56	
57	- `format_distance(km)` returns `f"{round(km, 1)} km"` ([`rides/view_model.py:4-6`](rides/view_model.py))
58	- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` both call it ([`rides/views.py:8`](rides/views.py), [`rides/views.py:16`](rides/views.py))
59	
60	### Check-in wizard
61	
62	**Location**: `wizard/`
63	
64	**What exists**:
65	
66	- Three `fieldset.question` elements; the second and third start `hidden` ([`wizard/wizard.html:5-19`](wizard/wizard.html))
67	- A click handler per answer button stores the value, hides the current question, and unhides the next ([`wizard/wizard.js:6-16`](wizard/wizard.js))
68	- No call to `focus()` and no `tabindex` handling anywhere in `wizard/`
69	
70	## Architecture Documentation
71	
72	**Current patterns found**:
73	
74	- Pages are plain string builders: `rides/views.py:6-17`
75	- Display formatting lives in `rides/view_model.py`, separate from the views
76	
77	**Component connections**:
78	
79	- `rides/views.py` → `rides/store.py`: listing (`rides/views.py:9`)
80	- `rides/views.py` → `rides/view_model.py`: distance text (`rides/views.py:8`)
81	
82	**Conventions observed**:
83	
84	- A ride is a dict with `date` and `km` keys.
85	
86	## Open Questions
87	
88	- None.

content.content:
1	---
2	project: rides
3	ticket: null
4	created: 2026-10-20
5	status: approved
6	last_updated: 2026-10-20
7	depends_on: research.md
8	design_approach: Fix the window constant, round half up in the view model, add a day total to the today page
9	---
10	
11	# Design: Rides Window, Distance Rounding, and Today's Total
12	
13	## Problem Statement
14	
15	README Goal (with the 2026-10-20 amendment): the rides page shows the last 28 days of rides inclusive, distances round half up, and the today page shows the day's total distance.
16	
17	1. **Rides window is one day short.** `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` and the cutoff `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` list today plus 26 prior days (`rides/store.py:4-10`). On Oct 28 a ride on Oct 1 is missing.
18	2. **Ties round to even.** `format_distance` uses built-in `round` (`rides/view_model.py:6`), so 12.25 km shows as 12.2 km where riders expect 12.3 km.
19	3. **No day total.** The today page lists each ride's distance and nothing else (`rides/views.py:14-17`).
20	
21	### Success Metrics
22	
23	- **M1**: On Oct 28 the rides page lists Oct 1 through Oct 28 inclusive. (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not (on Oct 28, a ride on Oct 1 is listed and one on Sep 30 is not)")
24	- **M2**: A distance exactly halfway between two tenths displays rounded up. (refines: amendment "distances round half up (12.25 km shows 12.3 km)")
25	- **M3**: The today page shows the sum of today's distances. (refines: amendment "the today page shows the day's total distance")
26	- Deferred: "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" (amendment: wizard work moves to a later project)
27	
28	## Design Approach
29	
30	- **Window**: change `WINDOW_DAYS` from 27 to 28 and keep the inclusive cutoff formula.
31	- **Rounding**: `format_distance` rounds through `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, converting the float with `str(km)` first. An `int` stays whole (`5` shows `5 km`) and a float keeps its one decimal (`10.0` shows `10.0 km`).
32	- **Day total**: `render_today_page` adds a `Total: <distance>` line after the list, formatted with `format_distance`.
33	
34	### Why This Approach
35	
36	- Each change is local to one function (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`; `rides/views.py:14-17`)
37	- Display formatting already lives in `rides/view_model.py`, so the total reuses it (research: Patterns)
38	- `Decimal(str(km))` rounds the decimal the rider entered. `Decimal(km)` would round the binary float, and a float such as 1.15 is stored just below 1.15
39	
40	## Technical Decisions
41	
42	### Architecture
43	
44	- Keep the string-built pages
45	  - Rationale: no page structure change beyond one line on the today page
46	  - Trade-off: none
47	  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`
48	
49	### Data Model
50	
51	- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`
52	
53	### Integration Points
54	
55	- `render_rides_page` picks up both the window and the rounding through its existing calls
56	- `render_today_page` gains the total line
57	
58	## Scope Definition
59	
60	### In Scope
61	
62	- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
63	- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`
64	- The day total on the today page
65	
66	### Out of Scope
67	
68	- The check-in wizard
69	- `load_series`
70	- Any new page
71	
72	## Success Criteria
73	
74	### Acceptance Criteria
75	
76	- **AC-1 A ride 27 days before today is listed on the rides page and one 28 days before is not**
77	  - Given today is 2026-10-28
78	  - When the rides page is rendered with rides on 2026-10-01 and 2026-09-30
79	  - Then the page lists the 2026-10-01 ride and not the 2026-09-30 ride
80	  - Example: rides on 2026-10-01 (10.0 km) and 2026-09-30 (8.0 km), today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `2026-10-01` and does not contain `2026-09-30`
81	  - Example (edge): a ride dated today, 2026-10-28, is listed
82	  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
83	  - Refines: M1
84	
85	- **AC-2 A distance halfway between two tenths rounds up on the rides page**
86	  - Given a ride today of 12.25 km
87	  - When the rides page is rendered
88	  - Then the ride shows as 12.3 km
89	  - Example: a ride on 2026-10-28 of 12.25 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `12.3 km`
90	  - Example (edge): a ride of 1.15 km shows as `1.2 km`
91	  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
92	  - Refines: M2
93	
94	- **AC-3 The today page shows the day's total distance**
95	  - Given rides today and on other days
96	  - When the today page is rendered
97	  - Then it shows the sum of today's distances only
98	  - Example: rides on 2026-10-28 of 10.0 km and 2.5 km and one on 2026-10-27 of 7.0 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `Total: 12.5 km`
99	  - Observed at: `render_today_page` HTML
100	  - Refines: M3
101	
102	### Harness Decisions
103	
104	| Boundary | Harness present? | Decision |
105	| --- | --- | --- |
106	| Rides page HTML (`render_rides_page`) | pytest (`pyproject.toml:10-12`, `tests/`) | Use as is |
107	| Today page HTML (`render_today_page`) | pytest (`tests/test_today_page.py`) | Use as is |
108	
109	### Non-Functional Requirements
110	
111	- [ ] Performance: no change
112	- [ ] Reliability: existing tests pass, except expectations this design changes
113	- [ ] Security: not applicable
114	
115	## Risk Analysis
116	
117	### Technical Risks
118	
119	| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
120	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
121	| Float values round unexpectedly | Low | Med | Convert with `Decimal(str(km))`; a test pins 1.15 → 1.2 km |
122	| A trailing `.0` is lost | Low | Low | Do not `normalize()` the Decimal; a test pins 10.0 → 10.0 km |
123	
124	### Assumptions
125	
126	- Distances are positive numbers.
127	
128	## Open Questions
129	
130	- None.
131	
132	## References
133	
134	- Research: [research.md](research.md)
135	- Intent: [README.md](README.md)
136
